drills.name: Dynamic Warm-Up Routine
drills.description: A full-team dynamic warm-up combining light movement, arm stretches, and activation exercises to get players ready to throw and field.
drills.setup: Players line up in two lines on the outfield grass. Lead through jog, high knees, butt kicks, shuffles, arm circles, and torso twists.
coachingPoints: Keep movements controlled — this isn't a race
Big arm circles forward and backward, at least 10 each direction
Finish with wrist circles and finger stretches

links.label: Youth Baseball Practice Warm-Up Routine
5 Dynamic Stretches for Baseball Warmup

drills.name: Partner Throwing Progression
drills.description: Partners start close (30 ft) and gradually work back to 90 ft, focusing on proper grip, arm path, and follow-through before any fielding work.
drills.setup: Pair players up. Start at 30 ft, throw for 2 min, back up to 60 ft for 2 min, back to 90 ft for remaining time. Rotate in any extras.
coachingPoints: Four-seam grip on every throw
Step toward your target — don't just arm it
Follow through: throwing hand should finish near opposite hip
Catch with two hands when possible

links.label: Youth Baseball: Simple Throwing Progressions
A Throwing Routine For All Youth Baseball Players

drills.name: Throwing Mechanics Breakdown
drills.description: Systematically breaks the throw into four checkpoints: grip, arm circle/path, hip-shoulder separation, and follow-through. Best for players who short-arm, rush, or have inconsistent accuracy. Run this slow before going full speed.
drills.setup: Players pair up at 45–60 ft. Coach walks through each phase with a demo, then players rep each phase 5x before putting it all together. Focus on feel, not velocity.
coachingPoints: Grip: four-seam grip across the wide seams — feel the two seams under the index and middle fingers
Arm path: ball goes down, back, and up in a smooth circle — think 'down and up', not 'back and sling'
Elbow stays at or above shoulder at the release point — low elbow = short-arm = inaccuracy
Hip-shoulder separation: hips turn first, shoulders follow — the throw starts in the legs, not the arm
Wrist snap is the last thing that fires — the ball should roll off your fingertips
Follow-through: throwing hand finishes near the opposite hip, back foot drags or lifts off the ground
For young players: cue 'show the ball to second base' as they break their hands to get the arm path right

links.label: Baseball Throwing Drills Youth Players MUST Be Doing
Youth Baseball Throwing Progression That Builds Athleticism
Throwing Mechanics Step-by-Step for Youth

drills.name: Wrist Snap & Arm Path Drill
drills.description: Isolates the wrist snap and release point — the most commonly skipped part of a youth player's throw. Done at short distance (10–15 ft) on a knee to remove legs from the equation entirely.
drills.setup: Players kneel on their throwing-side knee, partner 10–15 ft away. Throw using only the forearm and wrist — no body rotation. Focus purely on finger pressure and snap.
coachingPoints: Ball should roll off the fingertips with backspin — a wobbly or side-spinning throw means no wrist snap
Index and middle fingers are your gas pedal — they're the last things touching the ball
Squeeze fingers on top of the ball at release, not the side
You can also do this standing — no-step throws isolate the same thing
10 reps kneeling → 10 reps standing no-step → 10 reps full throw is a great warmup progression

links.label: Baseball Throwing Drills Youth Players MUST Be Doing

drills.name: Crow Hop to Target Drill
drills.description: Outfielders and corner infielders practice the crow hop — the footwork pattern that generates power on longer throws. Without a proper crow hop, outfield throws die short or sail high.
drills.setup: Two lines 80–100 ft apart. Player receives a toss or rolls to themselves, uses a crow hop, and fires to a partner or target cone at chest height. 8–10 reps per player.
coachingPoints: Crow hop pattern: catch → small replace step toward throwing arm side → hop onto the throwing-side foot → stride and throw
The hop generates momentum toward the target — you should feel yourself moving forward into the throw
Keep the throw low: chest-to-knee height on the fly. Low throw with a hop is faster than a rainbow
Don't death-grip the ball — a relaxed hand means a loose arm means more velocity
Outfielders: always crow hop before a relay throw, even on a short one — build the habit

links.label: Outfield Throwing & Crow Hop Mechanics

drills.name: Ground Ball Fundamentals (3-Step Method)
drills.description: Teaches the three fundamentals of fielding a ground ball: athletic ready position, approaching the ball (charge or wait), and fielding out front with soft hands.
drills.setup: Line players at short or third. Coach rolls or hits ground balls to each player. Rotate every 5-6 reps.
coachingPoints: Feet shoulder-width apart in ready position — stay on the balls of your feet
Field the ball out in front of your body, not underneath you
Funnel the ball toward your belly button with two hands
Eyes through the ball — watch it all the way into the glove

links.label: How to Field a Ground Ball in 3 Easy Steps
3 Simple Baseball Fielding Drills for Youth Players

drills.name: Short Hop Showdown
drills.description: Players partner up and take turns throwing short hops at each other from 20 ft. Develops soft hands and teaches players to stay low and committed on difficult hops.
drills.setup: Partners face each other at 20-25 ft. One player bounces the ball just in front of the fielder, forcing them to field a short hop. Switch roles every 10 reps.
coachingPoints: Get low — bend at the knees, not the waist
Soft hands: let the ball come to you, absorb it
Don't stab or swipe — stay patient
Keep your glove below the ball and let it come up into your glove

links.label: Fun Youth Baseball Drills (Short Hop Showdown at 3:32)

drills.name: Four Cone Ground Ball Drill
drills.description: Uses four cones in a square to force players to move laterally and charge ground balls from different angles, simulating real game situations.
drills.setup: Set four cones in a 10-foot square. Player starts at center. Coach rolls balls to different corners forcing the player to move, field, and reset.
coachingPoints: Move your feet first, then get your glove down
Always reset to center after each rep
Stay low through the entire fielding motion — don't stand up early
Quick feet on the lateral move, slow down as you approach the ball

links.label: Practice Fielding Ground Balls With Four Cones | Little League

drills.name: Alligator Traps
drills.description: Players practice snapping down on the ball with their glove like an alligator's jaw — a fun drill that prevents the classic 'flip-up' glove error on slow rollers.
drills.setup: Coach rolls slow balls toward fielder. Player approaches, gets glove flat, and snaps down on the ball. Works great as a station alongside other fielding reps.
coachingPoints: Glove starts flat on the grass, palm up — waiting for the ball
Snap the glove closed around the ball, don't scoop
This eliminates the habit of flipping the glove open-palm-up and praying
Great for slow rollers and bunts

links.label: Fun Youth Baseball Drills (Alligator Traps at :06)

drills.name: Pancake Glove Drill
drills.description: Players use a flat paddle/pancake glove (or just their bare hand) to field ground balls, forcing them to get their body in front, watch the ball all the way in, and use proper hand positioning. Eliminates lazy technique immediately — you can't cheat with a pancake glove.
drills.setup: Coach rolls or hits slow-to-medium ground balls to the fielder. Player uses a pancake glove or bare hand to field, then transfers to their regular glove for the throw. 6–8 reps per player, rotate through.
coachingPoints: Get your body in front of the ball — you can't reach and stab with a pancake glove
Watch the ball all the way into your hand — no looking up early
Field out front, slightly left of center (for righties) — not between your feet
Soft hands: absorb the ball, don't fight it
After the reps with pancake glove, the regular glove feels huge — use that confidence

links.label: Baseball Fielding Drills — Pancake Glove Drills

drills.name: Drop Step Fly Ball Drill
drills.description: Teaches outfielders the proper drop step to get a jump on balls hit over their head. One of the most critical skills for outfield development.
drills.setup: Coach stands 60-80 ft in front of two outfielders positioned side by side. Coach calls 'L' or 'R' or throws arms back indicating a deep fly ball. Player drop steps and sprints to spot before ball arrives.
coachingPoints: Drop step FIRST — turn your hips and go, don't backpedal
Get to the spot early: catch the ball while moving forward if possible
Track the ball over your throwing shoulder, not straight back
Call for it — 'I got it! I got it!' on every ball

links.label: 3 Great Baseball Outfield Drills for Youth Players
Baseball Outfield Drills You MUST Be Doing!

drills.name: Fly Ball Catching Progression
drills.description: A three-step progression for catching fly balls: track, position (glove above eyes, elbow bent), and catch with two hands on routine balls. Great for infielders who struggle with pop-ups too.
drills.setup: Coach hits or tosses fly balls from varying distances. Start with easy straight-up flies, progress to balls that require movement.
coachingPoints: Get your body behind the ball whenever possible
Catch at eye-level or above — not at your waist
Two hands for routine fly balls: bare hand guides the throw grip immediately
Call it loud and early so teammates know to back off

links.label: How to Practice Catching Fly Balls
3 Great Drills for Teaching Kids to Catch Fly Balls

drills.name: Outfield Two-Drill Circuit
drills.description: Two outfield-specific drills run back-to-back: (1) Closed-eye tracking drill for spatial awareness, (2) On-the-run catching for balls to either side.
drills.setup: Split outfielders into two lines. Run each drill for 6 minutes. Coach hits fungoes.
coachingPoints: Read the ball off the bat — hips, not hands
Crow hop before throwing back to infield
Stay relaxed — tight muscles mean bad reads on the ball

links.label: 2 Outfield Drills for Catching Fly Balls (Youth Players)

drills.name: First Base Footwork Drill
drills.description: Teaches the three primary footwork patterns for a first baseman: catch-and-step right, catch-and-stretch, and crossover for errant throws. One of the highest-impact drills for 12U teams.
drills.setup: Player at first base, coach or partner throws from each infield position. Practice stretching, staying on bag, and coming off bag for short-hops.
coachingPoints: Find the bag with your foot before the throw arrives — don't look down
Stretch toward the throw, not away from it
Off-target throws: come off the bag if you have to — an out isn't worth a bad stretch
Catch first. Tag second. Step off after the catch.

links.label: Youth Baseball 1st Base Footwork and Drills (Antonelli)
First Base Footwork Drills - Fundamentals (Part 1)
Skills Lesson: First Base Footwork

drills.name: Double Play Feed Drill
drills.description: Focused on the middle infield: SS and 2B practice receiving the feed, pivoting, and firing to first in time. One of the most skill-intensive plays in youth baseball.
drills.setup: SS and 2B at their positions. Coach hits ground balls to third or first. Middle infielders practice the feed to second and relay to first. Rotate SS and 2B roles.
coachingPoints: Get to the bag early — you need time to set your feet
Receive the throw, don't chase it
Short, quick throw to first — don't wind up
Pivot type depends on where the throw comes from: inside, outside, or straight on

links.label: How to Turn a Double Play — 3 Steps for Youth Players
Double Play Drills with Bill Ripken
Double Play Infield Tips and Drills (Antonelli Baseball)

drills.name: Cutoffs and Relays — Walk-Through
drills.description: Full-team walk-through of cutoff and relay positioning for 4 core scenarios: single to left, single to right, ball in the gap (double), and extra-base hit down the line. Walk through each scenario slowly before going live with baserunners. Critical for preventing extra bases — most youth runs score because nobody was in line.
drills.setup: Set up full defense + 1–2 baserunners. Coach hits or throws to each outfield zone. Stop and correct positioning before going live. Run each scenario 3–4 times total.
coachingPoints: Cutoff alignment: SS takes throws from LF/LC, 2B takes throws from RF/RC — communicate before the pitch
Cutoff man gets in a straight line between where the ball IS and where it's going — don't guess, move your feet until you're in line
Outfielder: throw through the cutoff at chest height. Think 'hit the target', not 'throw to the base'
Cutoff listens for verbal direction: 'CUT TWO!' means cut it and throw to second. 'CUT HOME!' means relay home. Silence = let it go
3B/P/C gives the verbal call — they have the full picture and can see the runner
Everyone NOT handling the ball has a job: backup the throw, cover a base, or get in trail position
Throw LOW: a low throw can be cut or hopped. A high throw can't be fixed

links.label: Cuts and Relay Drill
Little League Cuts and Relays Done Right
Pro Baseball Insider: Relay & Cutoff Fundamentals

drills.name: Double Cutoff (Two-Man Relay)
drills.description: Teaches the double cutoff (two-man relay) used on automatic doubles or any ball that gets past the outfielder. SS is the lead catcher; 2B is the trail. Focuses on alignment, spacing, and the trail man's communication role.
drills.setup: Full defense positioned for a double. Coach hits a gapper or ball down the line. SS positions as lead relay (40–50% of the way from OF to target base), 2B is trail 20–30 ft behind. Target is home or 3B depending on runners.
coachingPoints: Double cut rule: line up 3 bases ahead of where the lead runner started. Bases empty → play at 3B. Runner on 1B → play at home
Lead cutoff man (SS) expects to make the throw ~80% of the time — be ready
If the throw from the OF is short-hopped or in the dirt, let it go — trail man (2B) picks it up
Trail man's voice is the lead man's eyes: 'you got it!' = throw is on line, take it. 'Let it go!' = bad throw, I've got it
Both men stay in fair territory even if the ball is in foul territory — especially on the right field line (catcher needs to see the runner)
After catching, turn to your glove side for the quickest release — don't spin to the arm side

links.label: Little League Cuts and Relays Done Right
Pro Baseball Insider: Double Cut Setup & Rules

drills.name: Cutoff Decision Game
drills.description: Live reps with baserunners and a scoring element to teach the cutoff man to make the right decision — cut it or let it go — based on actual runner position. Turns the walk-through into a competitive game-like situation.
drills.setup: Full defense + 2 baserunners. Coach hits to the outfield. Baserunners run hard. The defensive player responsible for calling the play (3B, P, C) must make the verbal call out loud. Score 1 point for defense if runner is thrown out or held; 1 point for offense if they advance or score.
coachingPoints: The verbal caller (3B/C) must commit loudly — hesitation kills relay throws
Cutoff: if you don't hear a call, default to holding (cut and look) — don't guess
Practice both 'CUT!' (hold the runner) and 'let it go!' so players know what each sounds like at game speed
After the play, debrief: was the call right? Was the alignment right? Did everyone have a backup?
Rotate runners through so everyone learns the offensive side too — knowing where runners go helps fielders make smarter calls

links.label: How to Perform a Cut-Off Play // Youth Baseball
Summer Skills Camp Cut-off and Relay Talk

drills.name: Outfield Communication Drill
drills.description: Two or three outfielders practice calling for fly balls between them, establishing who has priority (center fielder rules), and backing each other up.
drills.setup: Two outfielders at their positions, 30-40 ft apart. Coach hits pop flies and gap shots forcing both players toward the same ball. One must call it; the other backs up.
coachingPoints: Center fielder has priority over corner outfielders — always
Call it twice and loud: 'Mine! Mine!'
If you don't hear a call — keep going. Don't just stop.
After the catch, communicate where the lead runner is

links.label: Top 5 Indoor Outfield Drills for Youth Baseball

drills.name: Situational Defense (Fungo)
drills.description: Coach hits with runners on base and announces the situation. Full defense must make the right play. Best closer for any fielding-focused practice.
drills.setup: Full defense takes the field. Place 1-2 base runners. Coach hits fungoes and calls the situation before each hit. Rotate runners and fielders throughout.
coachingPoints: Everyone on the field has a job on every play — no spectators
Back-up responsibilities are as important as the primary play
Talk it through before the pitch: 'Where am I going with this?'
Reset after each play — don't carry mistakes into the next one

drills.name: Belly Up Drill
drills.description: Players kneel with their belly toward the sky (back arched) and catch rolled balls while in that position, training the feel of soft hands and glove positioning below the ball.
drills.setup: Player lies back arched on their knees. Partner rolls or bounces balls so the fielder must field from underneath. 10 reps, then switch.
coachingPoints: This exaggerates the 'glove below the ball' position
You can't use your arm to compensate — pure hands work
Transfer the feeling: this is what 'soft hands' feels like in a normal position too

links.label: Fun Youth Baseball Drills (Belly Up at 1:10)

drills.name: Charging Slow Rollers
drills.description: Teaches infielders to read slow-rolling balls early, charge aggressively, and make an accurate throw on the run. A game-changer for third basemen and corner infielders.
drills.setup: Coach rolls slow balls toward the third base line or up the middle. Fielder must charge hard, field on the move, and throw to first. Focus is footwork and timing the fielding step.
coachingPoints: Read it fast — you have less time than you think
Right-handed fielder: field off the right foot to set up the throw
Don't field and then try to set — it's one fluid motion
If it's close, bare-hand it — don't be afraid to use your throwing hand

links.label: Youth Baseball Fielding Drill Young Players Will Love!

drills.name: Game-Like Drills for Efficient Practice
drills.description: A high-rep, game-speed team session that strings together fielding, throwing, and baserunning decisions in realistic game situations. Maximizes reps per minute with minimal standing around.
drills.setup: Full defense on the field. Coach hits or throws live balls with base runners in place. Players must read the ball, communicate, and execute — just like a real game. Rotate players every 5-7 minutes.
coachingPoints: Every rep should be game speed — no lazy warm-up throws
Communicate before and after every play: call the ball, call the base
Rotate positions so everyone gets reps in multiple spots
Debrief after each round: what did we do well, what needs work?

links.label: Game-Like Drills for Efficient Baseball Practice (Championship Productions)

drills.name: Relay Race Competition
drills.description: Teams compete to relay a ball from the outfield warning track to home plate in the fewest throws and fastest time. Combines conditioning, throwing accuracy, and fun competition.
drills.setup: Split team into two groups. Each group forms a relay line from center field to home. First player fields a ball and starts the relay. The team whose ball reaches home first wins the round.
coachingPoints: This is about quick releases and accurate throws, not arm strength
Stay in a straight line — off-line throws kill your time
Fielder who catches faces the next person in line before throwing
You should be able to do this in 3 throws from the warning track

drills.name: Triangle Drill
drills.description: A classic infield drill where the fielder moves through three positions — straight on, glove side, and throwing side — fielding a ball at each point of the triangle before returning to start. Builds footwork, lateral range, and consistent glove positioning.
drills.setup: Three balls placed in a triangle roughly 6-8 ft apart. Fielder starts at the top. Fields ball 1 straight on, shuffles to ball 2 on the glove side, shuffles to ball 3 on the throwing side. Fielder throws to partner or bucket after each catch.
coachingPoints: Stay in an athletic crouch throughout — don't stand up between balls
Shuffle feet laterally; avoid crossing your feet
Same fielding mechanics every rep: funnel, two hands, eyes through the ball
Great for pre-practice reps without needing a coach to throw

links.label: Baseball Infield Skills and Drills - The Triangle Drill (Ball State)
Triangle Drill (GGC Baseball)

drills.name: Backhand Ground Ball Drill
drills.description: Trains infielders to field balls to their throwing-hand (backhand) side — one of the hardest plays in youth baseball. Focuses on proper crossover step, glove angle, and making a strong throw from a difficult angle.
drills.setup: Coach rolls or hits balls to the fielder's backhand side (right side for right-handed). Fielder uses a crossover step, drops the glove low with fingers pointing down, fields the ball, plants, and fires to first.
coachingPoints: Crossover step first — don't reach across your body
Glove tilted so fingers point DOWN on the backhand, not sideways
Field off your right foot (RH fielder) to load into the throw
Short arm action on the throw — there's no time to wind up

links.label: How To Field a Ground Ball Backhand
Factory 101: Forehand & Backhand Athleticism

drills.name: Forehand Ground Ball Drill
drills.description: Trains infielders to field balls to their glove side (forehand). Works on the crossover step in the opposite direction, keeping the glove out front, and making a throw from open body position.
drills.setup: Coach rolls or hits balls to the fielder's glove side (left side for right-handed). Fielder uses a drop-step crossover, extends the glove out in front, fields, and throws to first.
coachingPoints: Get in front of the ball if possible — don't just arm reach
Glove side: field off your left foot (RH) to square up to first base
If you can't get in front, field off your right foot and make a quick flip
Head stays down through the catch — watch it into the glove

links.label: Factory 101: Forehand & Backhand Athleticism

drills.name: Catcher Blocking Drill
drills.description: Teaches catchers to block balls in the dirt with proper technique: drop to knees, chin down, glove between the legs, and body angle to funnel the ball in front of the plate.
drills.setup: Catcher in full gear at home plate. Coach or partner bounces balls directly in front, to the left, and to the right. Catcher blocks and locates the ball. Run 10 reps each direction.
coachingPoints: Drop straight down — don't dive forward or backward
Chin to chest to protect the throat and keep eyes on the ball
Glove fills the gap between the legs — don't let it sneak through
After blocking, find the ball immediately and be ready to throw

links.label: Top 5 Blocking Drills for Catchers

drills.name: Catcher Pop Time Drill
drills.description: Focuses on reducing the time from catch to throw for catchers throwing to second base. Emphasizes quick transfer from glove to throwing hand, efficient footwork, and a compact arm path.
drills.setup: Catcher in gear behind the plate. Coach throws live pitches or tosses from the mound. On each pitch, catcher receives, transfers, and throws to second (or a target at 2B distance).
coachingPoints: Transfer happens at the ear — don't drop the ball to the waist first
Replace your feet: throwing foot replaces catching foot in one quick hop
Stay low through the throw — standing up kills your accuracy
Grip the ball correctly in the transfer, not after the throw starts

links.label: How To Improve Catcher Pop Time

drills.name: Pitcher Fielding Practice (PFP)
drills.description: Pitchers practice fielding their position: bunts down the lines, comebackers, covering first base, and fielding slow rollers. One of the most undercoached areas in youth baseball.
drills.setup: Pitchers take turns throwing a pitch (or simulate it), then the coach rolls or hits a ball to a specific spot. Pitcher must field it and make the right throw. Run scenarios: bunt to third, bunt to first, comebacker, cover first on a ball to the right side.
coachingPoints: Finish the pitch in fielding position — balanced, head up
Charge the bunt aggressively — don't wait for it to come to you
On a comebacker: field, glance at the lead runner, throw to first
Cover first on any ball hit to the right side — sprint hard to the bag

links.label: How To: Pitcher's Fielding Practice (PFPs)
10 Types of Pitcher Fielding Practice (PFPs)

drills.name: Bunt Defense with Runners
drills.description: Full-team bunt defense drill with runners on base. Covers the two most common bunt scenarios at 12U: runner on first (sacrifice bunt) and runners on first and second (force at third).
drills.setup: Full defense + 1-2 base runners. Coach rolls a bunt out front. Defense must charge, communicate who has the ball, and make the correct throw. Walk through assignments first, then go live.
coachingPoints: Pitcher and corner infielders all charge — someone must call it
Catcher is the quarterback: call the play ('first!', 'third!')
Third baseman: if you're charging, SS covers third
On a hard bunt, you have more time than you think — be accurate

links.label: Bunt Defense | Runners on 1st and 2nd

drills.name: Leads and Secondary Leads
drills.description: Teaches proper primary and secondary leads at first, second, and third base. One of the highest-ROI skills for 12U — most runs are lost on baserunning, not hits.
drills.setup: Split team across the three bases. Walk through primary lead (2-3 shuffles off bag), secondary lead (2 shuffles on pitcher's motion), and reading the ball off the bat. Coach simulates pitch delivery.
coachingPoints: Primary lead: 2-3 shuffles, balanced athletic stance, weight forward
Secondary lead: 2 shuffle steps as the pitch crosses the plate
Read the ball in the dirt: freeze and wait — don't auto-advance
On a fly ball: tag up at 3B, hold at 1B/2B until you see it caught

links.label: Youth Practice Plan Series: Leads and Steals
Baseball Baserunner Leads and Reads from Second Base

drills.name: Crow Hop Throwing Drill (Outfield)
drills.description: Teaches outfielders to use a proper crow hop to generate momentum and arm strength on throws from the outfield. One of the most commonly skipped fundamentals at the youth level.
drills.setup: Outfielders line up in left-center. Coach hits or tosses fly balls. After the catch, player must execute a crow hop (replace throwing foot with glove-side foot, step, throw) before releasing the ball. Targets a cutoff or second base.
coachingPoints: Catch the ball, then immediately replace your feet — don't stand flat-footed
Crow hop is a forward skip: it loads your body toward the target
Throw through the cutoff's chest, not in a high arc
Point your glove shoulder at the target on release

links.label: 3 Great Baseball Outfield Drills for Youth Players

drills.name: Long Toss Progression
drills.description: A structured long toss program that builds arm strength and loosens the shoulder through gradually increasing distance. Best used 2-3x per week rather than every practice.
drills.setup: Partners start at 60 ft. Every 2 minutes, take one large step back. Progress to 90, 120, and up to 150 ft if arm feels good. Come back in gradually the same way.
coachingPoints: Never throw long toss on a cold arm — warm up with short catch first
At max distance, a slight arc is fine — don't strain to keep it flat
Come back in at the same pace you went out
If arm is fatigued or sore, stop early — this is a tool, not a test

links.label: A Throwing Routine For All Youth Baseball Players

drills.name: Rapid-Fire Infield Reps
drills.description: High-rep infield station where the coach hits 3-4 balls in quick succession to one fielder before rotating. Builds focus under fatigue and forces players to reset quickly between reps — great late in practice when attention drifts.
drills.setup: Fielder at position. Coach hits 3 balls in a row, each a different type: straight on, backhand, forehand. Fielder throws each to first or a partner. Coach immediately goes to the next player.
coachingPoints: Reset your feet between each ball — don't get lazy
This isn't about perfection, it's about staying locked in when tired
Communicate after each catch even in rapid fire
The third ball is always the test — that's when focus breaks

links.label: How To Work Through A Ground Ball + 4 Drills

drills.name: The 6 F's of Fielding
drills.description: A step-by-step framework for infield defense developed by MLB infield coach Perry Hill. Breaks down the entire ground ball sequence — from pre-pitch to throw — into six fundamentals every infielder must master. Great as a teaching drill or pre-practice walkthrough before live reps.
drills.setup: Walk players through each F individually before combining. Coach hits or rolls ground balls, calling out each phase. Can be done with no ball first (dry rep), then add ball.
coachingPoints: 1. Feet — Take a small step with the right foot and jump-stop into your ready stance, feet wide, staying low and moving as the ball enters the zone
2. Field — Get your glove out front and read the ball early; if you can't see your glove, you're too upright — field the ball out front, not beside you
3. Funnel — Bring the ball to your middle or chest; taking the ball to the side kills your balance and accuracy
4. Footwork — Footwork gets you into throwing position; a right-handed fielder loads off the right foot after fielding
5. Fire — Make a strong, accurate throw — four-seam grip when possible, step toward your target
6. Follow-through — Complete the throw, finish the motion, stay balanced; the play isn't done until the ball is caught

links.label: Mastering the 6 F's of Fielding (Coach Pete)

drills.name: Free Hitting
drills.description: Uncoached batting practice where players swing freely to integrate their skills and enjoy hitting without instruction.
drills.setup: Bucket of balls, coach or pitcher to throw live or feed a pitching machine at home plate.
coachingPoints: Resist the urge to coach during this drill — let players put it together on their own
Observe and note any corrections for later drill sessions
For older players, include bunts, hit-and-runs, and moving runners as options

drills.name: Goalie Game
drills.description: Hitters defend a hockey/lacrosse goal from balls pitched toward it, developing bat control and a short, contact-oriented swing.
drills.setup: Place a hockey or lacrosse goal as a backstop behind home plate. Use a pitching machine with softer balls or a tennis ball machine.
coachingPoints: Focus on making contact and directing the ball away from the goal
Encourage a short, compact swing to improve bat-to-ball contact
Can use coach-thrown pitches if machines aren't available
equipment: pitching machine or tennis ball machine

drills.name: Hitting Contests
drills.description: Add a competitive scoring element to standard hitting drills to boost engagement and focus on proper mechanics.
drills.setup: Bucket of balls and a coach or pitching machine. Scorecard for tracking points per player or team.
coachingPoints: Award points based on quality of contact — more for line drives, fewer for weak grounders
Design a point system around whatever concept you are currently teaching
Stress proper mechanics at all times; competition should reinforce good habits, not override them

drills.name: Knock Out the Catcher
drills.description: A coach in full catcher's gear sits on a chair close to home plate while hitters try to knock the coach off the chair, naturally encouraging up-the-middle hitting.
drills.setup: Coach wears full catcher's gear and sits on a chair or bucket 10–15 feet from home plate. Use soft or sponge rubber balls.
coachingPoints: If hitters are pulling off the ball, toss to the outside part of the plate to promote a better stride toward the pitcher
Keep coaching simple for young players; the fun element naturally teaches the concept
Watch for front shoulder flying open, which causes weak pull-side contact

drills.name: Line Drive Home Run Derby
drills.description: A home run derby format where only line drives count, teaching players to keep their head, eyes, and hands on the ball through contact.
drills.setup: Standard batting setup with a bucket of balls and a coach or machine to pitch. Set distance thresholds for what counts as a line drive.
coachingPoints: Only hard line drives score — pop-ups and weak grounders are eliminated
Focus on keeping head and eyes on the ball through contact
Reward players who use proper fundamentals even when they don't hit it perfectly

drills.name: Tee Hitting for Distance
drills.description: Players hit off a tee and compete to see how far they can drive the ball, reinforcing proper weight shift and a level or slightly downward swing path.
drills.setup: Batting tee at home plate, bucket of balls, optional cones or stakes to mark distance in the field.
coachingPoints: Emphasize weight shift going back before coming forward — 'go back to go forward'
Disqualify players who drop the back shoulder and try to uppercut; hard line drives and ground balls count
If players top the ball or hit the tee, the back shoulder is likely dropping — keep the barrel headed down to the ball

drills.name: Soft Toss
drills.description: A partner or coach tosses balls underhand from the side for hitters to drive into a net or screen, focusing on grip, bat speed, and a quick swing.
drills.setup: Bucket of balls, net or screen to hit into, tosser kneeling in foul territory slightly in front of the plate.
coachingPoints: Use a loose grip in the fingers with door-knocking knuckles lined up to promote wrist release and bat speed
Tosser should be in front and to the side, not directly across — balls coming straight at the hitter force an inside-out path
Verbal cue: 'Loose hands, quick bat'

drills.name: Tee Work
drills.description: Systematic hitting off a batting tee focusing entirely on developing proper weight shift and a downward swing path.
drills.setup: Batting tee adjusted so players must swing slightly downward to reach the ball. Net, screen, or fence to hit into.
coachingPoints: Focus on shifting weight to the back side before exploding forward — 'go back to go forward'
Keep the head down and eyes on the ball all the way through contact
If players top the ball or hit the tee, have them pick a spot on the ball and focus on it until contact

drills.name: Short Toss From the Front
drills.description: Coach tosses from in front of the hitter behind a screen, pitching to the outside part of the plate to encourage staying through the ball and using the big part of the field.
drills.setup: L-screen 10–12 feet in front of home plate, coach on stool or chair behind screen, bucket of balls.
coachingPoints: Hitters should keep the front shoulder in and drive the ball up the middle or the other way
Weakly pulled ground balls signal that the front shoulder is pulling out too early
Natural pull-side contact is fine if it produces hard line drives

drills.name: Stickball Drill
drills.description: Hitters use a thin stickball-type bat and small plastic balls to develop a quick, balanced swing without striding, reloading immediately for the next pitch.
drills.setup: Small plastic balls, thin stickball bat, tosser to flip balls in standard soft-toss position, net or screen to hit into.
coachingPoints: Have batters take their natural stride, stop at that position, then take the lower half out of the drill
Swing as hard as possible while reloading quickly — if they can't reload, they're off balance
Slow the pace if the batter is swinging late; let the batter set the tempo

drills.name: Bunting Drill
drills.description: Players practice sacrifice bunts aimed into target zones along the baselines set up with cones, keeping the ball away from the pitcher.
drills.setup: Four cones set in pairs down each baseline halfway between home and the mound. Bucket of balls, coach to pitch from shortened distance.
coachingPoints: Pivot both feet instead of squaring — start with bat at top of strike zone, barrel above hands
Give with the pitch to deaden the ball; use the bottom hand to guide direction
Leave pitches above the bat alone; bend the knees for lower pitches rather than dropping the barrel

drills.name: One-Arm Drill
drills.description: Hitters alternate between two-handed swings and single top-hand-off swings to develop a direct, short swing path to the ball.
drills.setup: L-screen 8–10 feet in front of batter, coach pitching overhand or underhand from behind screen, full-size bat.
coachingPoints: Hit five with two hands, then five with one, then five more with two hands
Let batters choke up or tuck the elbow into the side if they struggle to control the bat one-handed
One-arm reps should be challenging — that difficulty is the point

drills.name: Lob Toss
drills.description: Coach tosses balls with a high, slow-pitch arc from 20–40 feet away, teaching hitters to keep their weight loaded on the back foot until the last possible moment.
drills.setup: L-screen 20–40 feet in front of home plate (adjusted for player level), coach on stool or standing, bucket of balls.
coachingPoints: Let the ball travel as deep as possible before initiating the swing — verbal cue: 'Let it get deep'
Players shifting weight forward too soon should widen their stance and shorten their stride
Designed to build patience and stop early weight transfer

drills.name: Baserunning Relays
drills.description: Players compete in baserunning relay races around the bases to improve conditioning, proper base turns, and competitive spirit.
drills.setup: Standard baseball field with bases. Split team into relay groups.
coachingPoints: Focus on proper base-running turns — inside corner of each bag, push off with the bag like a starting block
Compete relay-style to add energy and motivation
Use as conditioning at the end of practice without it feeling like punishment

drills.name: Big League Baserunning
drills.description: Players run through common game situations — single to first, double, scoring from second — emphasizing proper turns and using the bag as a push-off point.
drills.setup: Full field with bases (pegged bases preferred). Players line up at home plate.
coachingPoints: Hit the inside corner of each base and use it to push off toward the next base like a starting block
Work through multiple scenarios: home-to-first through the bag, first-to-third turn, run out a double, score from second
Set up cones to mark the proper rounding path for players who struggle with their routes

drills.name: Head to Head
drills.description: One player starts at home running to second while another starts at second running home, showing that smart base running beats raw speed.
drills.setup: Field with bases (pegged preferred). Coach stands on pitcher's mound to give the 'Go' signal.
coachingPoints: Player from home simulates running out a double; player from second simulates scoring on a hit
Emphasize that fundamentals and proper turns often beat a faster runner who takes poor routes
Highlight players who use good fundamentals when they win

drills.name: Slip and Slide Sliding Drill
drills.description: Players practice proper sliding mechanics on a slip-and-slide to learn technique in a safe, fun environment without risk of injury.
drills.setup: Slip-and-slide on soft grass with a hose for water and a base placed at the end.
coachingPoints: Slide on the butt, not the hips — keeps toes pointed up instead of sideways
Avoid head-first slides in training, though you can let players try it for fun at the end
Great way to end a hot practice — players naturally stay engaged

drills.name: Cutoff Relay Race
drills.description: Teams race to relay a ball from the outfield to home using proper cutoff mechanics, blending competition with throwing fundamentals.
drills.setup: Two or more teams lined up in relay positions across the outfield. Ball starts in the outfield and must reach home plate through the relay chain.
coachingPoints: Turn toward the glove side — never toward the throwing arm side — when receiving a relay
Catch the ball while already moving toward the next target to stay in rhythm
Accurate throws on a line beat long, looping ones even in a race

drills.name: Long-Toss Golf
drills.description: Players throw at cone targets in a golf-style game, building arm strength while focusing on throwing accuracy and arc.
drills.setup: Cones placed at challenging distances in the outfield as 'pins,' with circles drawn or taped around them as 'greens.' Each player gets 25–50 throws.
coachingPoints: Throw with a slight arc to build carry and arm strength — not a flat line or a pop-up
Keep shoulders on the same plane throughout the delivery
An accurate one- or two-hop throw scores better than a longer off-target one

drills.name: Shoot and Score
drills.description: Players throw at small goals across from each other, earning points for goals scored in the air or on a roll to develop throwing accuracy.
drills.setup: Two goals set up at a throwing distance players can handle. Players stand beside each goal and take turns throwing at the other's goal.
coachingPoints: Award 1 point for a ball rolling into the goal and 2 for a ball entering in the air
Optional: hang a target inside the goal for a bonus scoring layer
Check mechanics when accuracy breaks down: grip, front shoulder, elbow height, follow-through

drills.name: Throw for Distance
drills.description: Players throw from a baseline as far as possible, then shuffle their feet and follow their throw to see how momentum adds distance.
drills.setup: Football field or any marked field with a clear distance reference. Bucket of balls. Cones or stakes to mark throws (optional).
coachingPoints: Demonstrate how shuffling and following the throw generates extra distance through momentum
Keep shoulders on the same plane — no excessive back shoulder drop
Do this drill only once per week to protect young arms

drills.name: Twenty-One
drills.description: A catch game where throws earn points based on where they're caught — chest-level earns 1, head-level earns 2 — with the first player to 21 winning.
drills.setup: Two players and a baseball at a comfortable throwing distance.
coachingPoints: Award points to the thrower even if the receiver drops an accurate throw
Can play to 15 to speed things up or set up a bracket-style team tournament
Stress proper mechanics on every throw — this is not just a warm-up game

drills.name: Other Throwing Games
drills.description: A flexible drill format where coaches create targets on fences, walls, or screens to turn any accuracy drill into a competitive game.
drills.setup: Bucket of balls and any target — painted on a fence, a batting tee to knock over, or a hanging screen target.
coachingPoints: Any target that demands concentration counts — knock a ball off a tee, hit a painted circle, score into a goal
Emphasize the full throwing chain: four-seam grip, elbow up, front shoulder toward target, step and follow through
When accuracy suffers, check grip, front shoulder alignment, elbow height, and follow-through

drills.name: One-Knee Drill
drills.description: Players drop to one knee and play catch at short distance to isolate and reinforce proper arm action — ball down, out, and up with the elbow above the shoulder.
drills.setup: Two players (or player and coach) facing each other at short distance. Throwing-side knee down, opposite knee up.
coachingPoints: Ball comes down, out, and up from the glove; hand stays on top of the ball as it leaves the glove
Elbow must stay above the shoulder at all times — 'pie throwing' with palm up is the most common error
Younger players can use soft baseballs and do the drill with a coach

drills.name: Tee Drill (Throwing)
drills.description: Players use a batting tee as a visual checkpoint, placing their arm in the power position at tee height to reinforce proper elbow elevation and hand placement.
drills.setup: Batting tee set at shoulder height, pairs of players facing each other at short distance.
coachingPoints: Use the tee to check that the hand is above and behind the ball at the power position — not under or beside it
Elbow should be at or above the level of the tee (shoulder height)
Check that the front shoulder points toward the target before the arm moves forward

drills.name: Power Position Drill
drills.description: Pitchers and players learn to throw from a wide-base power position, focusing on grip, hand placement, elbow height, and weight transfer without a full wind-up.
drills.setup: Pairs of players (pitcher and catcher optional) facing each other. Mound optional. Baseball.
coachingPoints: Wide base, weight shifts back before moving forward; hand above the ball with fingers away from target at power position
Elbow must be above the shoulder before the arm swings forward; front shoulder points at target
Trail foot stays in contact with the rubber and rotates; front toe points forward at finish

drills.name: Long Toss
drills.description: Partners gradually move apart with each throw, challenging arm strength by throwing with a slight arc at maximum comfortable distance.
drills.setup: Two players and a baseball. Start close, move back a few steps with each throw until the distance is challenging.
coachingPoints: Throw with a slight arc to build carry — not a pop-up loft, not a flat line
Keep shoulders on the same plane; one-hop arrivals are fine
Once arms begin to fatigue, move closer to finish; pitchers do this between starts

drills.name: Balance Position Drill
drills.description: Pitchers pause for a three-count at the balance position before delivering to the plate, learning to gather energy before committing forward.
drills.setup: Pitcher throwing from a mound (or flat ground) to a catcher at shortened distance. Work from the stretch.
coachingPoints: At balance position: leg slightly closed, butt toward catcher, glove at knee level, body not leaning back
Hold the count of 3 before striding — this forces the body and arm to travel forward together
Common error is leaning the upper body backward, which throws off timing

drills.name: Toe Tap Drill (1-2-3 Drill)
drills.description: Pitchers tap the stride foot down twice before throwing on the third count, building back-leg strength, balance, and a soft, controlled landing.
drills.setup: Pitcher throwing from mound or flat ground to a catcher at shortened distance.
coachingPoints: Count: tap down (1), tap down (2), stride and throw (3)
Stay balanced and controlled — avoid landing with a hard stomp that disrupts timing
Shoulders should remain fairly level; avoid abruptly changing planes when the foot lands

drills.name: Pitcher Covering First Base Drill
drills.description: Pitchers practice sprinting to cover first base on ground balls to the right side, taking a proper path and receiving the underhand flip from the first baseman.
drills.setup: Pitchers and first basemen in position. Coach at home plate with fungo and balls. Catcher in place. Optional second baseman.
coachingPoints: Sprint to a point about 10–12 feet from the bag, then turn and run parallel to the baseline
Hold the glove at chest level as a target; catch the ball first, then find the bag
Coach mixes in comebackers to keep pitchers alert; never jog or take a direct path to the bag

drills.name: Comebacker Drill
drills.description: Pitchers throw a pitch and then field a ball rolled or hit back to them, working on finishing in fielding position and making accurate throws to first base.
drills.setup: Pitchers behind the mound, first basemen at first. Coach at home plate with fungo or roll. Catcher in place.
coachingPoints: Pitcher must finish the pitch in a balanced fielding position before reacting to the ball
Field it, step toward first, and follow the throw — not as dramatic a follow-through as a normal infielder
Can also use this drill to work on double plays started by the pitcher

drills.name: Pitcher Bunt Fielding Drill
drills.description: Pitchers practice fielding bunt placements to both sides of the infield, learning the footwork to create momentum toward their target before throwing.
drills.setup: Pitchers behind mound, first basemen at first, catcher in place. Coach rolls bunts from home plate after each pitch.
coachingPoints: Right-hander on first-base side: open toward first before fielding to generate momentum toward target
Left-hander on first-base side: left foot between ball and foul line, rotate to glove side before throwing
Reverse footwork for third-base-side bunts; add batters for realism and combine with player bunting practice

drills.name: Lite Flite Elimination
drills.description: Players compete to catch foam or lite-flite balls thrown by a coach, with missed catches leading to elimination until one player remains.
drills.setup: Coach throws or tosses lite-flite balls at varying heights and distances. All fielders start in a group; misses eliminate that player.
coachingPoints: Catch with two hands above the head, watching the ball all the way into the glove
Get to the spot early rather than drifting under the ball
Safe balls prevent injury while still building the same catching habits as with hard baseballs

drills.name: Pass Patterns
drills.description: A coach acts as quarterback while outfielders run crossover and drop-step routes, making over-the-shoulder catches like football receivers.
drills.setup: Coach (or long-toss pitcher) as quarterback. Outfielders line up and toss ball to quarterback before running their route.
coachingPoints: Crossover step: pivot the near foot while crossing the far foot over it in the direction of the ball
Drop step: step back toward a ball hit over the head, then cross over in the direction of the ball
Restart immediately if the initial step is wrong — the first step is everything

drills.name: Thrown Fly Balls
drills.description: Coach throws fly balls by hand so players practice catching them properly with two hands above the head in a controlled setting before transitioning to batted balls.
drills.setup: Bucket of balls, coach to throw varying heights. Use soft or sponge rubber balls for beginners.
coachingPoints: Catch with two hands above the head so eyes can track the ball all the way into the glove
Get to the spot early and catch while moving slightly forward — not backpedaling
Start with short, easy tosses and increase height gradually as confidence builds
equipment: bucket of balls (soft balls for beginners)

drills.name: Thrown or Machine Ground Balls
drills.description: Coach throws or uses a pitching machine to deliver ground balls to outfielders, building proper fielding posture before transitioning to batted balls.
drills.setup: Coach throwing or pitching machine aimed at outfielders. Bucket of balls.
coachingPoints: Field with a wide base, butt down, hands out in front
Glove fingers pointing down with wrist relaxed to absorb bad hops
Build confidence with controlled throws before moving to fungo-hit ground balls

drills.name: Communication Drill
drills.description: Two outfielders converge on a fly ball hit between them and practice calling for the ball clearly, with the calling player making the catch and the other providing backup.
drills.setup: Two lines of outfielders at least 20 feet apart. Coach throws or hits fly balls between the two. Optional cutoff player for throws.
coachingPoints: The player taking the ball calls 'I got it!' at least three times clearly
If two players call simultaneously, the one who continues calling should take the ball
Designate a centerfielder with priority on any ball they can reach as players advance

drills.name: Crossover Step Drill
drills.description: Outfielders practice the crossover step to the coach's direction and then receive a thrown ball to develop the most efficient lateral movement on the field.
drills.setup: Outfielders lined up. Each player tosses ball to coach, assumes ready position, and coach signals the direction before throwing.
coachingPoints: Pivot the foot nearest the ball's direction while crossing the far foot over it — not a drop step
Stop the drill immediately and restart if the first step is wrong
The crossover step applies equally to baserunners, infielders, and outfielders

drills.name: Drop Step Drill
drills.description: Outfielders practice the drop step to get back on balls hit over their heads, receiving a throw directly overhead after executing the footwork correctly.
drills.setup: Outfielders lined up. Each tosses ball to coach, assumes ready position, coach says 'Go,' player drops one foot back and crosses over before coach throws directly overhead.
coachingPoints: Step back first with the foot on the side the ball is going, then cross over in that direction
Stop and restart if the initial step is wrong — footwork habits are built through repetition
Catch with two hands above the head; over-the-shoulder catches come from Pass Patterns

drills.name: Machine Fly Balls
drills.description: A pitching machine throws high fly balls to outfielders at consistent height and location, allowing repetitions that force players to move forward to catch the ball.
drills.setup: Pitching machine set to throw fly balls at desired height. Bucket of balls. Coach feeds machine. Use soft balls if players aren't confident.
coachingPoints: Machine fly balls fall nearly straight down at the peak — players must read the spin and adjust
Do not use hard baseballs until players are confident enough with the skill
Key benefit: forces players to learn to catch while moving forward rather than drifting back

drills.name: Fence Drill
drills.description: Outfielders sprint back toward the warning track, locate the fence with their throwing hand, and catch a fly ball near the wall to develop safe fence awareness.
drills.setup: Coach throws fly balls that will land near the warning track. Outfield fence or wall required. Bucket of balls.
coachingPoints: Glance back once to locate the fence visually, then keep eyes on the ball
Feel for the fence with the bare throwing hand once on the warning track
Catch with two hands above the head — the goal is safe play, not home-run robberies

drills.name: Hitting Balls to Outfielders
drills.description: Coach uses a fungo to hit fly balls and ground balls to outfielders, giving them a realistic look at balls coming off a bat rather than being thrown.
drills.setup: Fungo bat, bucket of balls, coach to hit, player or coach to receive throws from outfielders.
coachingPoints: Adapt speed and height to each player's skill level — don't hit balls too hard or too high until players are ready
Repetitions are the key for outfielder development once fundamentals are in place
Hard baseballs should only come after players are comfortable with softer balls

drills.name: Rolled Ground Balls
drills.description: A coach or player rolls slow ground balls to infielders at close range, allowing players to focus entirely on proper glove position and fielding footwork.
drills.setup: Coach or player kneeling close to fielder, rolling controlled ground balls directly to the glove. Bucket of balls.
coachingPoints: Glove fingers pointing nearly straight down with wrist relaxed — glove out in front of the body
If the ball isn't staying in the glove, check glove angle; have the player scrape dirt forward with the glove to find the proper out-in-front position
Relaxed wrist helps read bad hops early and adjust the glove accordingly

drills.name: Throwing After the Catch Drill
drills.description: Infielders field ground balls and then use cones to guide them through the proper path of generating momentum toward their target before throwing.
drills.setup: Three cones in a line toward the target (simulating a 5-4 force play). Coach rolls ground balls, player or coach receives throws.
coachingPoints: Catch first, then move toward the target — momentum toward the throw produces stronger, more accurate throws
Stay low through the shuffle; standing up before throwing causes high or low misses
Follow the throw past the second cone

drills.name: Throwing-Side Foot Backhand Drill
drills.description: Infielders practice the backhand technique for hard-hit balls slightly to their throwing-hand side by setting the right leg and dropping the left knee to create a wide, low base.
drills.setup: Coach rolls balls at close range directly into the glove on the throwing-hand side. Cones for alignment (optional).
coachingPoints: Right leg extended with instep facing the coach; left knee drops to the ground — creates wide, low base
Glove placed in front of the right foot and open toward the coach — catch out in front
Progress to rolling balls slightly outside the planted foot once players get comfortable

drills.name: Glove-Side Foot Backhand Drill
drills.description: Infielders practice the extended backhand for balls farther to their throwing-hand side by crossing the glove-side leg over in a lunge position.
drills.setup: Coach rolls balls slightly in front of the extended lead foot. Cones optional. Players go one at a time, five reps each.
coachingPoints: Glove-side leg crosses over the other leg as if walking past; throwing-side knee drops in a lunge
Ball is caught off the front foot (not directly in front of it) — glove-hand wrist stays relaxed and open
Avoid twisting the glove — squeeze the ball when it enters and bring it straight to the chest

drills.name: High Five Drill (Underhand Flip)
drills.description: Infielders field rolled ground balls and execute an underhand flip toward a coach, finishing by walking through and giving the coach a high five to reinforce keeping the hand high.
drills.setup: Coach 10–15 feet away rolling ground balls. Players in fielding position with wide base and hands in front.
coachingPoints: Catch first, generate momentum toward target, flip underhand with hand finishing high at head level
Walk through after the flip and give the coach a 'high five' — wherever the hand ends up is where the ball goes
Keeping the hand high after the flip is the single most common thing to correct

drills.name: Box Drill – Short to Second
drills.description: Players form a box and practice the underhand flip from the shortstop angle, shuffling and flipping to the left while following through to the next corner.
drills.setup: Four players at corners of a 25-foot (or smaller) box, fifth player as extra at one corner. No gloves to improve concentration.
coachingPoints: Each player faces the corner to their right; shuffle or crossover, flip, leave hand high, follow to the next corner
No gloves — bare hands force better focus on catch-and-release
Use softer balls or gloves for younger players who need more confidence

drills.name: Box Drill – Second to Short
drills.description: Players form a box and practice the awkward front-of-body underhand flip used by second basemen feeding shortstop, keeping the hand and wrist stiff without turning the body.
drills.setup: Four players at corners of a 25-foot (or smaller) box, fifth player as extra at one corner. No gloves to improve concentration.
coachingPoints: Each player faces the corner to their left; hand stays in front of the body without the body fully turning
Keep the wrist stiff and avoid turning the torso so the hand stays in front — awkward but correct
Use gloves or softer balls for younger players

drills.name: 4-6 / 6-4 Double Play Drill
drills.description: Shortstops and second basemen alternate feeding each other on force plays at second base, working on the underhand flip and the receiving footwork at the bag.
drills.setup: One group at shortstop, one at second base. Coach rolls ground balls from between home plate and the mound. First basemen optional to complete the double play.
coachingPoints: 6-4: shortstop fields and flips; second baseman arrives early, left foot on bag, takes right foot toward the ball
4-6: reversed — shortstop covers with right foot on bag and takes left foot toward the ball
Player covering second must arrive as a stationary target before the flip arrives

drills.name: First Base Receiving Drill
drills.description: First basemen practice receiving throws from around the infield, learning the timing of stretching the glove and glove-side foot toward the ball simultaneously.
drills.setup: Coach anywhere in the infield throwing to first basemen who alternate on the bag. Empty bucket near first base for players to put retrieved balls in.
coachingPoints: Heel of the throwing-side foot on the bag at setup; square shoulders to the thrower
Take glove and glove-side foot toward the ball at the same time — do not stretch early
Stay tall and react to errant throws rather than premature stretching

drills.name: Backhand Throwing Drill
drills.description: Infielders range to backhand ground balls, stop their momentum, shuffle back to a starting cone, and then make a controlled throw — avoiding off-balance off-momentum throws.
drills.setup: Two cones set up for each player. Player starts at cone 1; coach rolls backhand ground balls. Player throws to coach or target past cone 2.
coachingPoints: Field the ball on the backhand, stop momentum going away from target, shuffle back toward target before throwing
Never throw off-balance — regain footing first
Stopping momentum moving away from the target is the hardest concept to build into habit

drills.name: Machine Backhands and Forehands
drills.description: A pitching machine rolls hard ground balls at a cone while players set up to the side and must break and field on the backhand or forehand without getting in front of the ball.
drills.setup: Pitching machine aimed at a cone. Players set up to one side so they must extend on a backhand or forehand to reach the ball at the cone. Alternate sides.
coachingPoints: Break as the ball is fed; catch out in front at the cone on backhand or forehand
Beginners may break early to set up before the ball arrives until they get comfortable
Can be turned into an elimination contest

drills.name: Machine Short Hops
drills.description: A pitching machine fires hard short-hop ground balls for fielders to catch with a proper glove angle and soft hands, optionally using bare hands or sponge balls for extra challenge.
drills.setup: Pitching machine set to throw fast balls on short hops. Soft/sponge rubber balls or regular baseballs. Wide base, butt down, hands out front.
coachingPoints: Relax wrist and catch out in front; try catching with one hand to encourage proper glove angle
Using soft balls and bare hands provides the ultimate challenge and the softest hands
Contest: see who can catch the most out of 5 or 10 consecutive short hops
equipment: bucket of balls (soft or sponge balls optional)

drills.name: Hitting Ground Balls to Infielders
drills.description: Coach uses a fungo bat to hit ground balls to infielders at game-like speed and angles, with players going 'live' to first after building confidence with individual reps.
drills.setup: Fungo bat and bucket of balls. Two coaches maximizes reps: one hits to third/short from first-base side, one hits to second/first from third-base side.
coachingPoints: Adapt speed to each player's skill and field conditions — bad hops on a rough field build no good habits
Run a live phase where fielders throw to first after collecting reps without throws
Older players can hit ground balls to each other if coaches are scarce
